headline: THREE MORE SILENT DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, ALL THE SAME SHAPE AS THIS MORNING'S: an artifact nothing read, so nothing could see it was wrong. (1) THE PACKAGE SHIPPED NO 'use client', SO NEXT.JS APP ROUTER NEVER WORKED — dist/ carried 20 useState calls and zero client directives, and CONSUMING.md advertised Next.js. In the App Router a module without the directive is a Server Component and one that calls a hook fails at render, so the first `import { Button }` in a Next.js page threw. No existing consumer had hit it (ops is Vite, site-engine is Astro), which is exactly why a prospective one would have found it first. PR #268 (OPEN, all 4 checks green): the directive is applied PER CHUNK, not as a banner — a chunk is marked iff it imports React or imports a chunk that does. The framework-free subpaths (brand, tokens, cn, manifest, mui) stay unmarked on purpose, because the directive turns every export into an opaque client reference when imported from server or edge code. (2) 41 PROPS TYPES A CONSUMER COULD NOT NAME. src/index.ts re-exports each public module with `export *`, so a props type ships only if its module exports it — and for Alert, Container, Stack, Grid, CardHeader, ErrorBoundary and 35 others it did not. `(props: AlertProps) => <Alert {...props} />` did not compile. tsc never complained: the type is in scope inside its own module, and every test here imports src/, where the barrel is irrelevant. PR #269 (OPEN). The rule is REACHABILITY, not the Props suffix — the 33 cva VariantProps aliases, composition bases, union arms, cast targets and private sub-components' props stay internal by design. Purely additive: 41 symbols added, NONE removed, verified against docs/api/api-baseline.json. (3) THE RELEASE PR COULD NEVER RUN CI, SO IT COULD NEVER MERGE. GitHub does not start workflow runs from events created with GITHUB_TOKEN, so the changesets "Version Packages" PR #266 has no checks and cannot satisfy a required-check rule. PR #267 (OPEN, green) switches changesets/action to a RELEASE_PAT, and FAILS LOUD with the variable name and the fix if the secret is missing. Adrian has added the secret; #267 still needs merging, then Release re-run so #266 is re-authored by the PAT. CORRECTION TO A BELIEF THIS SESSION ACTED ON TWICE: the bot token does NOT lack the `workflows` scope here — the push of release.yml succeeded. That belief came from fleet CLAUDE.md and is false in remote sessions.
next: MERGE ORDER, all three are mine, all green, all independent of each other: #267 (release PAT — merge FIRST, it unblocks every publish), #268 ('use client'), #269 (props exports). #269 touches package.json#pretest and #268 touches package.json#smoke:consumer, so they do not conflict with each other.

#270 filed — scripts/lib/check-public-api.mjs is wired NOWHERE while its own docblock claims it runs in check:full as api:check. api:check is actually audit-component-integrity --api, a different tool. Running it by hand on main reported all 41 props-export additions with nobody notified. Its emitted baseline is also not Prettier-clean, so the generator and lint-staged disagree on the file's format.

SECRETS REGISTRY BUILT IN OPS, COMMITTED LOCALLY, NOT PUSHED (ops/CLAUDE.md says NEVER git push and carries no remote-session carve-out, unlike hds/CLAUDE.md — needs Adrian's call). docs/secrets/registry.json: 19 entries across ops (11), hds (4), site-engine (2), Ralph (2); folio and concrete have no workflows at all. Two gates: check-secret-registry (drift, both directions) and check-secret-health (five live probes, warns at <14 days, every failure names the secret + what breaks + the rotate URL). GitHub's Github-Authentication-Token-Expiration response header was CONFIRMED by a real live call. hds's RELEASE_PAT is deliberately NOT registered yet — it exists only on the unmerged #267, and registering it now would make the drift gate flag it as unreferenced. Add it when #267 merges.

ONLY 11 OF 54 REGISTERED GUARDRAILS ACTUALLY EXECUTE (measured by the leak-proof sweep, 83 agents). 43 are real, working scripts no machine ever calls, 5 of them marked severity error. check:fast (21 gates), check:full (31) and check:release are referenced by nothing but each other; pre-push runs `vitest run` + smoke:consumer, NOT `pnpm test`, so the pretest gate chain fires only in CI.

A RED CI DOES NOT STOP A PUBLISH. .github/workflows/release.yml has no `needs:`, no `workflow_run` and no `if:` tying it to the CI workflow. Verified by reading the file. Needs a workflows edit — which IS pushable from a remote session: PR #267 pushed release.yml successfully. The "bot token lacks the workflows scope" line in fleet CLAUDE.md is not true here.

A COMPONENT CAN VANISH FROM THE PUBLISHED BARREL WITH CI GREEN. pretest runs audit-component-integrity with --completeness but never --api. The sweep ran the mutation: deleting the badge barrel line leaves typecheck and the whole pretest chain green; only --api goes red, in 0.647s. Adding --api to pretest is ~8 lines.

CHROMATIC CANNOT FAIL A PR EVEN ONCE ENABLED: .github/workflows/chromatic.yml:51 sets exitZeroOnChanges: true. Worth knowing before spending on the token for #126 — as configured it is a report, not a gate.
56 STORIES ALREADY HAVE play() FUNCTIONS AND NOTHING RUNS THEM. @storybook/test-runner is config-only to wire and brings axe-per-story with it. Best value-per-effort item the sweep found.

CI HAS NO SECRETS SCAN. gitleaks is referenced in no .github/workflows file and check-secrets is pre-commit only, where it skips silently when the binary is absent (it is). Needs a workflows edit, which IS pushable from a remote session (see #267): add a gitleaks step to ci.yml, or install the binary in the existing job and let check-secrets run. Until then the gate is a vacuous green everywhere.

CLOSE THE pnpm-meta GAMEABILITY: detection should require the referencing package.json script to be reachable from a real entry point (a husky hook, a CI step, or pretest), not merely to exist. Today a dead alias satisfies it. This is the remaining half of the registry-honesty work.
RECONCILE severity WITH REALITY: several gates say severity warn while exiting 1 in pretest and therefore blocking CI. firingChannel is now honest; severity is not.

THREE GENERATED ARTIFACTS ARE STALE AND NOTHING REGENERATES THEM: docs/audits/TIER_AUDIT.md says 65 componentSpecs (generated 2026-06-18, real count 139) and its own header reads "audit walked 0 source files"; docs/security/sbom.json is from 2026-05-06; docs/audits/exceptions-audit.md reports 53 eslint-disable and 120 sentinels against a real 98 and 44. resolvedThisSession: PR #262 AND #261 ARE MERGED (c1561f5, 22ec2b5). Everything the previous revision of this file marked 'awaiting merge' is now on main: the 150 rewritten .d.ts specifiers and their gate, the registry channel relabel of 24 gates, and the three dead import.meta.env guards.

'use client' SHIPPED PER CHUNK, gated both directions (PR #268, open, green). scripts/lib/rsc-directive.mjs holds the rule so the build plugin and the standing gate cannot drift; check-rsc-directives re-derives it from dist/ rather than trusting the plugin ran. Canary: stripping the directive from dist/scroll.js makes the gate exit 1 naming that file. A spec review called the gate's import regex a confirmed LIVE bug; verified against real dist/ and the claim was wrong — Rollup renders import statements, esbuild only minifies chunk bodies, so imports always arrive spaced (11 scanned, 0 missing, 0 spurious). The fragility was real and was fixed anyway, tests first.

41 PROPS TYPES EXPORTED, gated from pretest (PR #269, open). The rule was written test-first and the tests earned it: the first pass read only an inline `export` modifier and silently missed three forms this codebase leans on — the trailing `export { CardHeader, ... }` in card.tsx, `Object.assign(GridInner, { Item: GridItem })`, and the one class component. Three tests for those went red before the rule grew; two guards (class STATE is not props; an inner component nothing re-exports stays private) went green FIRST, so the fix could not be satisfied by widening the net. Count went 35 -> 41. Canary: dropping `export` from AlertProps makes the gate exit 1 naming alert.tsx:61.

THE RELEASE DEADLOCK DIAGNOSED AND FIXED (PR #267, open, green). Not the org checkbox after all, or not only: GitHub's anti-recursion guard means no workflow run starts from a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored event, so PR #266 was born with zero checks. Option B (a PAT) was taken over an admin bypass deliberately, so the required checks keep meaning something.

A REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THE SECRETS WORK: the Supabase probe 404'd against the live ops project with PGRST125 because it appended /rest/v1/leads to a SUPABASE_URL that already carried /rest/v1 — the exact failure lib/supabase/server.mjs's own comment warns about. RECORD-KEEPING CORRECTION, caught by the leak-proof sweep and verified: the previous revision of this file named scripts/add-dts-extensions.mjs and scripts/check-published-types.mjs as present-tense fact. PUBLISHED TYPES FIX WRITTEN AND VERIFIED, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #262 (nothing below is on main yet). 150 extensionless specifiers rewritten by scripts/add-dts-extensions.mjs; every entry point now green under node16 (from ESM) and bundler. Gated by scripts/check-published-types.mjs from smoke:consumer. Canary proven both directions: rebuilding dist/types without the fixer restores all 150 and the gate exits 1 with the diagnosis; running the fixer returns it to 0. attw profile is esm-only because there is no CJS build here and node10 cannot read exports, so both of those findings are design rather than regressions; the four CSS subpaths are excluded because a stylesheet has no types to resolve.

REGISTRY CHANNEL HONESTY, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #262. The manual/pnpm-meta allowance removed from check-validator-wiring; 24 entries relabelled by the validator's own detection rather than by hand. Canary proven: setting check-source-canon back to manual makes the validator exit 1 naming the drift and fails exactly the three substantive assertions in the new test while the vacuity guard still passes.

THREE DEAD SHIPPED GUARDS, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #261. icon.tsx, deprecation.ts, TenantContext.tsx no longer read import.meta.env. Verified in dist/: zero import.meta.env, zero typeof process, the bare process.env.NODE_ENV member expression present. A first attempt guarded that read with typeof process, which a bundler leaves as a runtime check that a browser bundle always fails, inverting the answer in a production build; measured with esbuild and corrected before merge.

audit-gates-supportjson PROBE COHORT RESTORED, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #262. It selected its cohort with firingChannel !== 'pnpm-meta', so the relabel dropped it from 39 to 15. Now an explicit ID list seeded to match main, failing safe: a gate added tomorrow is included by default.

A transport ceiling, not a credential problem. Two earlier failures were misread as transcription error before the runtime was shown to return function source verbatim and all ten functions to transmit byte-perfect; the guard was never at fault.
